messages:
alexandra.sre: Heads-up: scheduled maintenance window for AZ-2 next Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. This is a capacity cutover + traffic-shift dry run, not a full outage. Purpose: validate our automated region failover and warm KV cache behavior. Please read the checklist below and ack if you need to opt out. :loud_sound:

mike.ops: Ack. I'll be on-call for the traffic-shift. Will watch pod drain rates and GPU pool metrics.

julia.observability: We're enabling higher retention for traces in that window (6h -> 24h) and turning on debug sampling for router to capture 1% of requests. Will push dashboard link shortly.

alexandra.sre: TL;DR checklist:
- Control plane: no changes (control-plane HA stays)
- Data plane: shift ~30% GA traffic from AZ-2 -> AZ-1 over 10m using router-weight schedule
- KV cache: pre-warm prefix list A/B before shift
- Fallback: if p95 token latency increases > 250ms for >5m -> rollback immediately
- Post-run: run ./scripts/verify-routing.sh and attach output

alexandra.sre: Router weights (example):
```
# at t0
az2: 70
az1: 30
# over 10m
az2: 40
az1: 60
# at +10m
az2: 30
az1: 70
```

kevin-oncall: Noted. I'll set an alert around p95 token latency and queue length. Can you confirm the exact query used for the alert?

julia.observability: Using the usual query: `sum(rate(token_latency_ms_bucket[1m])) by (le)` then compute p95 with histogram_quantile(0.95, ...). I'll paste it to #eng-sre-alerting in 5.

deploy-bot: Reminder: no model deploys to AZ-2 between 01:00-05:00 UTC on Tue (automated block applied).

alexandra.sre: Important: this is a DR rehearsal only — we are NOT failing AZ-2. We're simulating capacity constraints by shifting traffic. If any service reports degraded performance, we either pause the shift (manual) or rollback to original weights.

mike.ops: Quick question — do we want to include Dedicated customers in the shift, or exclude reserved pools?

alexandra.sre: Exclude reserved Dedicated pools and any pinning groups. We'll annotate the shift to ignore tenant_pools with tag `dedicated:reserved`. I'll update the runbook.

julia.observability: Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/ops/az2-dryrun (will be live 30m before window). Also created a Grafana panel that overlays p95 with cache hit rate.

kevin-oncall: I'll be on-call from 01:45-04:30 UTC. If p95 spike persists after rollback for >15m, escalate to infra@redwood and trigger postmortem drill.

alexandra.sre: Post-run tasks (owners):
- kevin-oncall: run failback verification and CPU/GPU scheduling checks
- julia.observability: capture trace samples, heap profiles for runtimes showing GC spikes
- mike.ops: collect kernel and network logs from AZ-2 nodes (snapshot)
- alexandra.sre: run the SLA sanity checks and publish results to #sre-status

incidents-bot: Scheduled event created: AZ-2 capacity cutover dry run. ID: E-2026-0421-az2-dryrun. On-call: kevin-oncall.

mike.ops: Acked. I'll bring the 'hotfix' team on standby for 30m after the run.

alexandra.sre: Thanks team — please react with :thumbsup: once you read and understood your action items. If you have scheduling conflicts, DM me today.

kevin-oncall: :thumbsup:

julia.observability: :thumbsup:

mike.ops: :thumbsup:

alexandra.sre: One more note — we'll coordinate a short 15m retro 2 hours after the window to capture learnings. Calendar invite will follow.

mike.ops: Sounds good.

julia.observability: See you there.
